mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, exalted is He, {يَا أَيهَا النَّاس}: أي is a singular vocative (nidāʾ mufrad), and therefore it takes ḍamma; its ḍamma is indeclinability (bināʾ), not inflection, and its position is the position of the accusative, because it is an object in meaning. النَّاس is a naʿt (adjective) of أي, and it is a naʿt that cannot be dispensed with, because it is the one addressed in meaning. According to Sībawayh it is not permitted to make it accusative according to the position, as is permitted in يَا زيد الظريف and الظريف [in the accusative] according to the position, because that is a naʿt that can be dispensed with. Al-Akhfash said: النَّاس is a ṣila (relative complement) of أي, and therefore it is permitted neither to omit it nor to make it accusative. Al-Māzinī permitted making النَّاس accusative by analogy with يَا زيد الظريف.
His saying {والأرحام}: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to the name of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "and fear [Allah regarding] the wombs, lest you sever them" (وَاتَّقوا الْأَرْحَام أَن تقطعوها). It may also be conjoined to the position of بِهِ, as you say مَرَرْت بزيد وعمرا ("I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr"), conjoining it to the position of بزيد, because it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in the position of the accusative; the verb was merely weak, so it became transitive through a particle. Whoever reads it in the genitive conjoins it to the hāʾ in بِهِ, and that is ugly according to Sībawayh, because the genitive pronoun is in the status of the tanwīn, since it alternates with the tanwīn in the like of غلامي وغلامك وداري ودارك and so on. What shows that it is like the tanwīn is that they dropped the yāʾ in the vocative, since that is a place from which the tanwīn is dropped: you say يَا غُلَام أقبل ("O my boy, come forward"). So you do not conjoin to what stands in the place of the tanwīn, just as you do not conjoin to the tanwīn. Al-Māzinī said: just as the first is not conjoined to the second, since it cannot stand alone after the conjunction, likewise the second is not conjoined to the first; they are two partners, and nothing is permitted in one of them except what is permitted in the other.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {مَا طَابَ لكم}: ما with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "so marry the good," meaning the lawful. ما is used for what is not rational and for the attributes of what is rational; for this reason it occurs here for the attribute of what is rational.
His saying {مثنى وَثَلَاث وَربَاع}: مثنى is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for ما. It is a diptote because it is shifted (maʿdūl) from اثْنَيْنِ, indicating repetition, and because it is shifted from a feminine, since number is feminine. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is a diptote because it is shifted from the meaning of the genitive construct (iḍāfa), and there is in it the implied entry of the alif and lām; and it was permitted to be declined (ṣarf) in number on the basis that it is indefinite. Al-Akhfash said: if you name [someone] with it, you decline it as both definite and indefinite, because the shifting has left it. It has been said: it is a diptote because it is shifted from its wording and from its meaning. It has been said: it is barred from declension because it is shifted and because it is an adjective. It has been said: it is barred because it is shifted and because it is a plural. And it has been said: it is barred because it is shifted and because it was shifted contrary to the principle of shifting, since shifting in principle is only for definites, and this is indefinite after the shifting. ثَلَاث and ربَاع are like مثنى in all its causes.
His saying {فَوَاحِدَة}: whoever reads it in the accusative, its meaning is "then marry one" (فانكحوا وَاحِدَة). Al-Aʿraj read it in the nominative on the implied form "then one suffices" (فَوَاحِدَة تقنع), so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted.
His saying {أَو مَا ملكت أَيْمَانكُم}: conjoined to فَوَاحِدَة in both readings together. مَا ملكت is a maṣdar, and therefore ما is used for those who are rational, for it is for an attribute of those who are rational.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying {نحلة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it has also been said that it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying {هَنِيئًا مريئا}: two ḥāls from the hāʾ in فكلوه. You say هنأني ومرأني, but if you use مرأني on its own you can only say أمرأني. The nominative pronoun in فكلوه refers to the husbands, and it has been said to the guardians; and the hāʾ in فكلوه refers to شَيْء.
His saying {قيمًا}: whoever reads it without alif makes it the plural of قيمَة. What shows this is that it underwent weakening, its wāw turning into yāʾ because of the kasra before it; had it been a maṣdar it would not have been weakened, just as الْحول and العور were not weakened. So its meaning is: "which Allah has made for you a support (قيمَة) for your goods and livelihoods." He said وَالَّتِي and did not say اللَّاتِي only because it is a plural of what is not rational, so it runs on the wording of the singular, as He said فَمَا أغنت عَنْهُم آلِهَتهم الَّتِي and said جنَّات عدن الَّتِي. Had it been for what is rational He would have said اللَّاتِي, as He said وربائبكم اللَّاتِي, وأمهاتكم اللَّاتِي and وَالْقَوَاعِد من النِّسَاء اللَّاتِي. This is what is most frequent in the speech of the Arabs; but اللَّاتِي may be used for what is not rational and الَّتِي for what is rational. It has been read أَمْوَالكُم اللَّاتِي, with the plural. Whoever reads قيَاما makes it a noun from أَقَامَ الشَّيْء ("he set the thing upright"), or, if you wish, a maṣdar of قام يقوم قيَاما; قوام also occurs in its sense, and it is not weakened. Al-Akhfash said: there are three dialectal forms of it: الْقيام, القوام and القيم — as though he made [the reading of] whoever reads قيمًا a maṣdar too.
His saying {نفسا}: tafsīr (specification). Fronting it is not permitted at all according to Sībawayh; al-Mubarrad and al-Māzinī permitted it when the governing word is fully conjugable.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {إسرافا}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it has also been said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). بدارا is like it.
His saying {أَن يكبروا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by بدار.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {نَصِيبا مَفْرُوضًا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial); it has also been said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {فارزقوهم مِنْهُ}: the hāʾ refers to what is divided (الْمَقْسُوم), because the word "division" (الْقِسْمَة) indicates it.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying {للذّكر مثل حَظّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative, as a clarification and explanation of the bequest.
His saying {فَإِن كن نسَاء فَوق اثْنَتَيْنِ}: in كَانَ is its noun (ism), and نسَاء is its khabar; its implied form is "if those left behind are women, more than two" (فَإِن كَانَ المتروكات نسَاء فَوق اثْنَتَيْنِ). The two daughters were given two-thirds only by the Sunna and by the indication of the text concerning the two sisters that they receive two-thirds; there is no indication in the text here that they take two-thirds, but in the text stating two-thirds for the two sisters there is an indication, since Allah made the single sister like the single daughter and made clear that the two sisters receive two-thirds, and was silent about the two daughters; so they were treated according to the ruling on the two sisters, by the evidence of the text and the Sunna.
His saying {وَإِن كَانَت وَاحِدَة}: whoever reads it in the nominative makes كَانَ complete (tāmma), not needing a khabar, in the sense of "occurred, came to be," so وَاحِدَة is nominative by its verb; this is the reading of Nāfiʿ alone. Whoever makes وَاحِدَة accusative makes كَانَ the deficient one (nāqiṣa) that needs a khabar, so he makes وَاحِدَة its khabar and implies its noun in كَانَ; its implied form is "and if the one left behind is one [daughter]" (وان كَانَت المتروكة وَاحِدَة).
His saying {السُّدس}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and what precedes it is its khabar. Likewise الثُّلُث and السُّدُس, likewise نصف مَا ترك, likewise فلكم الرّبع, likewise فَلَهُنَّ الرّبع, فلهن الثّمن and فلكل وَاحِد مِنْهُمَا السُّدس.
His saying {من بعد وَصِيَّة يُوصي بهَا أَو دين}: i.e. a bequest with no debt with it, because the debt is what takes precedence over the bequest.
His saying {نفعا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification).
His saying {فَرِيضَة من الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {وَإِن كَانَ رجل يُورث كَلَالَة}: كَانَ is in the sense of "occurred" (وقع), يُورث is a naʿt (adjective) of رجل, رجل is nominative by كَانَ, and كَلَالَة is accusative as tafsīr (specification). It has been said that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that كلالة is the deceased, in these two views. It has been said that it is accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "is inherited from by an inheritance of كلالة" (يُورث وراثة كَلَالَة), on the basis that كلالة is the property that neither child nor parent inherits; this is the view of ʿAṭāʾ. And it has been said that it is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, on the basis that كلالة is a name for the heirs, its implied form being "possessing كلالة" (ذَا كَلَالَة). As for whoever reads يُورِث with kasra on the rāʾ, or with kasra and doubling (يُورِّث), كَلَالَة is the object of يُورث, and كَانَ is in the sense of "occurred."
His saying {غير مضار}: accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in يُوصي.
His saying {وَصِيَّة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying {تجْرِي من تحتهَا الْأَنْهَار}: the clause is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
His saying {خَالِدين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in يدْخلهُ; it is plural only because it is construed according to the meaning of من.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {خَالِدا فِيهَا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in يدْخلهُ; it is singular because it is construed according to the wording of من. If you made خَالِدا a naʿt (adjective) of نار, it would be permitted in speech, but you would make overt the pronoun that is in خَالِد and say خَالِدا هُوَ فِيهَا. You will see the principle of this explained.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {واللذان يأتيانها مِنْكُم}: the preferred choice according to Sībawayh for اللَّذَان is the nominative, even though the meaning of the statement is a command, because when الَّذِي is completed by a verb the meaning of condition becomes established in it, since it does not refer to a specific thing. Once condition and vagueness are established in it, it runs the course of a condition, so an implied verb preceding it does not govern it, just as what precedes a condition, implied or overt, does not govern it. Since it is far-fetched for an implied verb preceding اللذين to govern them, implying [a verb] is not good; and since implying the verb before them to make them accusative is not good, they are nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), just as you make the condition nominative. The accusative is permitted on the assumption of an implied verb, because it merely resembles a condition, and what resembles a thing is not like the thing in its ruling. If you completed الَّذين with an adverbial phrase, its resemblance to a condition would become remote, and the accusative would become the preferred choice when the statement has the meaning of command or prohibition, as in your saying اللَّذين عنْدك فأكرمهما ("the two who are with you, honour them"): the accusative is the preferred choice in it, and the nominative is permitted. In what is completed by a verb, the nominative is the preferred choice, and the accusative is permitted on an implied verb explained by the khabar (predicate); it is ugly for it to be explained by what is in the ṣila (relative clause). If you omitted the hāʾ from the khabar, its governing اللذين would not be good, because the fāʾ prevents that, since what follows it is cut off from what precedes it.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {أَن ترثوا النِّسَاء كرها}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by يحل. It is a prohibition against marrying a woman under compulsion. This was something the people of the Jāhiliyya used to do: the son or the relative would have more right to the wife of the deceased than anyone else, even if the woman disliked that. كرها is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and like it is بهتانا.
His saying {إِلَّا أَن يَأْتِين}: أَن is an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ laysa min al-awwal), in the position of the accusative.
His saying {فَعَسَى أَن تكْرهُوا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by عسى, because its meaning is "your dislike of something has drawn near, while Allah has placed much good in it"; so أَن with the verb is a maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying {إِلَّا مَا قد سلف}: ما is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
His saying {وَأَن تجمعُوا بَين الْأُخْتَيْنِ}: أَن is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to أُمَّهَاتكُم, i.e. "and combining two sisters has been forbidden to you" (وَحرم عَلَيْكُم الْجمع بَين الْأُخْتَيْنِ). Likewise وَالْمُحصنَات is nominative, conjoined to أُمَّهَاتكُم.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying {كتاب الله عَلَيْكُم}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the view of Sībawayh, because when He said حرمت عَلَيْكُم أُمَّهَاتكُم it was known that this is prescribed, so it is as though He said "Allah has prescribed it for you as a prescription" (كتب الله عَلَيْكُم كتابا). The Kufans said it is accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ) through عَلَيْكُم; that is far-fetched, because what is accusative by ighrāʾ does not precede what stands in the place of the verb, namely عَلَيْكُم, and here it has preceded. Had the text been عَلَيْكُم كتاب الله, making it accusative by ighrāʾ would have been better than [making it] a maṣdar.
His saying {إِلَّا مَا ملكت أَيْمَانكُم}: ما is in the position of the accusative as an exception, and مَا ملكت is a maṣdar; therefore ما is used for those who are rational, because what is meant by it is an attribute of those who are rational. ما is used to ask about what is not rational and about the attributes of those who are rational.
His saying {أَن تَبْتَغُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for ما in His saying مَا وَرَاء ذَلِكُم; or in the position of the nominative, according to the reading of whoever reads وَأُحِلّ in the passive, also as a badal for ما.
His saying {محصنين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تَبْتَغُوا; likewise غير مسافحين.
His saying {فَمَا استمتعتم بِهِ}: ما is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a conditional; its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَآتُوهُنَّ, which is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.
His saying {فَرِيضَة}: a ḥāl; it has also been said: a maṣdar in the position of the ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying {أَن ينْكح}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition; its implied form is إِلَى أَن ينْكح ("to marry") or لِأَن ينْكح ("for marrying").
His saying {محصنات}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and nūn in مِنْهُنَّ; likewise غير مسافحات, and likewise وَلَا متخذات أخدان.
His saying {ذَلِك لمن خشِي الْعَنَت}: ذَلِك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is its khabar (predicate), i.e. "the concession to marry slave-women is for whoever fears hardship."
His saying {وَإِن تصبروا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and خير is its khabar; its implied form is "and patience in refraining from marrying slave-women is better for you." «[Translator's note: the quotation is written وَإِن in the source, while the comment treats it as أَن (the Quranic text is وَأَن تَصْبِرُوا); translated as written.]»

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {ضَعِيفا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. he was created such that his desire, his appetite, his anger and his contentment overcome him, so he needed Allah to lighten [things] for him.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying {إِلَّا أَن تكون تِجَارَة}: whoever reads it in the nominative makes كَانَ complete (tāmma), in the sense of "occurred." Whoever reads it in the accusative makes it the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ and implies its noun in كَانَ; its implied form is "unless the property is property of trade" (إِلَّا أَن تكون الْأَمْوَال أَمْوَال تِجَارَة), then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. It has also been said that its implied form is "unless the trade is a trade" (إِلَّا أَن تكون التِّجَارَة تِجَارَة). The first implied form is better because of the prior mention of "property." أَن in His saying إِلَّا أَن is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Like تِجَارَة in nominative and accusative is His saying وان تَكُ حَسَنَة.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {عُدْوانًا وظلما}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He said "transgressing, doing wrong" (مُتَعَدِّيا ظَالِما).

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {مدخلًا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun). Whoever reads the mīm with fatḥa makes it the maṣdar of دخل, and whoever reads it with ḍamma makes it the maṣdar of أَدخل; and His saying ندخلكم points to أَدخل.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {وَلكُل جعلنَا}: the muḍāf ilayhi is omitted along with كل; its implied form is "and for every one" (وَلكُل أحد) or "[every] soul" (نفس). It has also been said that its implied form is "and for everything that the parents and the nearest relatives leave, We have made mawālī," i.e. heirs to it.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {بِمَا حفظ الله}: i.e. by Allah's guarding of them. Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read الله in the accusative (الله), with the meaning "by their guarding [the right of] Allah" (بحفظهن الله). His saying واهجروهن فِي الْمضَاجِع: فِي الْمضَاجِع is not an adverbial for the forsaking; it is only the cause of the staying away. Its meaning is: "and forsake them because of their staying away from lying with you."

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {الَّذين يَبْخلُونَ}: in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for من in His saying لَا يحب من كَانَ.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying {رئاء النَّاس}: رئاء is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذين; then وَلَا يُؤمنُونَ بِاللَّه is cut off, not conjoined to يُنْفقُونَ, because a ḥāl from الَّذين is not included in its ṣila (relative clause), so you would be separating the ṣila from the relative noun by the ḥāl if you conjoined وَلَا يُؤمنُونَ to يُنْفقُونَ. If you made it a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in يُنْفقُونَ, it would be permitted for وَلَا يُؤمنُونَ to be conjoined to يُنْفقُونَ, included in the ṣila, because the ḥāl [then] is included in the ṣila of الَّذين, since it is a ḥāl of what is in the ṣila. «[Translator's note: the source's final clause literally says «because the ḥāl from الَّذين is included in the ṣila»; the sense is the ḥāl from the pronoun within the ṣila.]»

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His saying {شَهِيدا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in بك.
His saying {يَوْمئِذٍ}: what governs it is يود. «[Translator's note: the source has a stray «ق» before this line.]»

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His saying {وَأَنْتُم سكارى}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تقربُوا. وَلَا جنبا is also a ḥāl from it, and likewise إِلَّا عابري سَبِيل, in the sense of "except travellers," so you perform tayammum for the prayer and pray while you are in a state of janāba. It has also been said that its meaning is "except passing through," on the basis that by "the prayer" the place of prayer is meant.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {يشْتَرونَ الضَّلَالَة}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذين, and like it is ويريدون.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t:
His saying {وَكفى بِاللَّه}: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and الله is in the position of the nominative by كفى. The bāʾ was added with the agent only so that the statement conveys the meaning of a command, because it is in the place of "suffice yourselves with Allah" (اكتفوا بِاللَّه), and the bāʾ indicates this meaning.
His saying {وليا} {ونصيرا}: two tafsīrs (specifications), or, if you wish, two ḥāls.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t:
His saying {من الَّذين هادوا}: من is attached to نصير, i.e. "suffice yourselves with Allah as a helper for you against those who are Jews." يحرفُونَ is then a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذين هادوا, so you do not pause at نَصِيرًا on this view. It has been said that من الَّذين هادوا is attached to an omitted element that is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "among those who are Jews are people who distort" (من الَّذين هادوا قوم يحرفُونَ); so من is attached to an omitted element, just as prepositions are attached when they are predicates — the explanation of this principle has already passed — and يحرفُونَ is a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted mubtadaʾ; so you pause at نَصِيرًا on this view. It has been said that من is attached to الَّذين أُوتُوا نَصِيبا من الْكتاب, making clear that they are among those who are Jews; so one does not pause at نَصِيرًا on this view either. And it has been said that the implied form is "among those [who are Jews] are some who distort the words" (من الَّذين من يحرف الْكَلم), so من is an omitted mubtadaʾ and من الَّذين هادوا is a fronted khabar; so you pause at نَصِيرًا on this view. Like it in the omission of من is His saying وَمَا منا إِلَّا لَهُ مقَام مَعْلُوم, i.e. "except one who has a known station" (من لَهُ مقَام مَعْلُوم).
His saying {غير مسمع}: accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in واسمع. What was intended in their intentions — may Allah curse them — was "and hear, may you not hear" (واسمع لاسمعت); they make it appear that by this wording they only mean "and hear, without being made to hear anything disliked." It has also been said that they mean "without being heard by you," i.e. without being answered.
His saying {ليا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun), originally لوي, then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ. It has also been said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and like it is وطعنا فِي الدّين.
His saying {وَلَو أَنهم قَالُوا}: أَن after لو is always in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ according to Sībawayh. Sībawayh did not permit a mubtadaʾ to occur [after لو] except with أَن specifically, because of the presence of the verb's wording after أَن; if a noun occurs after لو, it is nominative by an implied verb according to him. Others said: أَن and other [nouns] are nominative after لو only by an implied verb.
His saying {إِلَّا قَلِيلا}: a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "except with little faith" (إِلَّا إِيمَانًا قَلِيلا). It is little only because they persist in [disbelief] and because their inner state is contrary to what they show. Had it been an exception, the proper course would have been to make قَلِيل nominative as a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in يُؤمنُونَ. If you made it excepted from لعنهم, it would not be good, because whoever disbelieves is cursed; none of them is excepted.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {كَمَا لعنا}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); its implied form is "a cursing like Our cursing of the people of the Sabbath" (لعنا مثل لعنتنا لأَصْحَاب السبت).

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying {سَبِيلا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification). Our saying "accusative as tafsīr" and "as tamyīz (specification)" are the same, except that tamyīz is used for numbers.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {فَإِذا لَا يُؤْتونَ}: according to the skilled grammarians it is not permitted to write إِذا except with nūn (إذن), because it is like لن, and there is no tanwīn in particles; al-Farrāʾ permitted writing it with alif. إذن here is cancelled (mulghāh), not governing, because the conjunction fāʾ has entered upon it. It is what puts the verb in the accusative according to Sībawayh when it does so; and according to al-Khalīl what puts it in the accusative is an implied أَن.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t:
His saying {من آمن بِهِ} and وَمن صد عَنهُ: both are a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes each mubtadaʾ is its khabar (predicate).
His saying {سعيرا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification).

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying {كلما نَضِجَتْ جُلُودهمْ}: what puts كلما in the accusative is His saying بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t:
His saying {تجْرِي من تحتهَا}: in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنات.
His saying {خَالِدين فِيهَا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in سندخلهم.
His saying {لَهُم فِيهَا أَزوَاج}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is لَهُم; the clause admits, as to its grammatical position, what خَالِدين فِيهَا admits.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {أَن تُؤَدُّوا} {أَن تحكموا}: أَن in both is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition; its original form is بِأَن تُؤَدُّوا and بِأَن تحكموا.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {وأولي الْأَمر}: the singular of أولي is ذَا used as a muḍāf, because it is accusative; the singular of أولو is ذُو, not from its own wording; likewise the singular of أولات is ذَات.
His saying {تَأْوِيلا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification).

mekki-muskil:61-61.t: His saying {صدودا}: a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) according to al-Khalīl, the maṣdar being الصد; so it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:66-66.t:
His saying {إِلَّا قَلِيل}: nominative as a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in فَعَلُوهُ. Ibn ʿĀmir read it in the accusative as an exception; that is far-fetched in negation, but it is so, with alif, in the copies of the Muṣḥaf of the people of Syria.
His saying {تثبيتا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification).

mekki-muskil:68-68.t: His saying {صراطا}: the second mafʿūl (object) of هدينا.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t: His saying {رَفِيقًا} and عليما: two tafsīrs (specifications). Al-Akhfash said: رَفِيقًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). أُولَئِكَ is in the position of the nominative by حسن.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t: His saying {فانفروا ثبات أَو انفروا جَمِيعًا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent pronoun in انفروا in both phrases. ثبات means "separately"; its singular is ثبة, and its diminutive is ثبية. As for ثبة of the basin, which is its middle, its diminutive is ثويبة.

mekki-muskil:73-73.t:
His saying {فأفوز فوزا}: its accusative is as the answer to the wish in His saying يَا لَيْتَني كنت مَعَهم.
His saying {كَأَن لم تكن بَيْنكُم وَبَينه مَوَدَّة}: a parenthesis between the saying and what is said; it is not part of the speech of the one who lagged behind from jihād, and what is meant by it is postponement, after the answer to the wish. مَوَدَّة is the noun (ism) of تكن and بَيْنكُم is the khabar (predicate). It is not good for يكون to be in the sense of "occur" (يَقع), because the meaning of the statement is not complete without بَيْنكُم وَبَينه; so it is the khabar, and by it the meaning is complete.

mekki-muskil:75-75.t:
His saying {وَمَا لكم لَا تقاتلون فِي سَبِيل الله}: لَا تقاتلون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from لكم, as you say مَالك قَائِما ("why are you standing?"), and as Allah said فَمَا لكم فِي الْمُنَافِقين فئتين and فما لَهُم عَن التَّذْكِرَة معرضين. ما in all of that is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the genitive phrase is its khabar (predicate).
His saying {وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ}: conjoined to the name of Allah, in the position of the genitive; it has also been said that it is conjoined to سَبِيل.
His saying {الظَّالِم أَهلهَا}: a naʿt (adjective) of القرية. This is permitted, although the wrongdoing is not the town's, because of the pronoun in its naʿt referring back to it. It is singular only because it runs on a singular noun and because there is no pronoun in it, since it has made an overt noun after it nominative, namely الأهل. Had there been a pronoun in it, it would not be permitted to be latent and it would have become overt, because the active participle, when it is a khabar, an adjective or a ḥāl for someone other than the one to whom it belongs, never has a latent pronoun in it at all, and it must be made overt; likewise if it is conjoined to someone other than the one to whom it belongs. The verb is the opposite of that: the pronoun is latent in it because of its strength, even if it is a khabar, an adjective or a ḥāl for someone other than the one to whom it belongs. So understand it, for it is a difficult, rare point of subtle meaning.

mekki-muskil:77-77.t:
His saying {إِذا فريق مِنْهُم}: فريق is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); مِنْهُم is a naʿt (adjective) of فريق in the position of the nominative; and يخشون is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.
His saying {كخشية الله}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); its implied form is "a fear like their fear of Allah" (خشيَة مثل خشيتهم الله).
His saying {أَو أَشد}: accusative, conjoined to the kāf.

mekki-muskil:78-78.t: His saying {أَيْنَمَا}: أين is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) containing the meaning of interrogation and condition; ما entered so that the condition would be established and become good. تكونوا is jussive by the condition, and يدرككم is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

mekki-muskil:79-79.t:
His saying {مَا أَصَابَك من حَسَنَة} {وَمَا أَصَابَك من سَيِّئَة}: ما in both is in the sense of الَّذِي ("that which") and is not conditional, because it was revealed concerning a specific thing, namely drought and abundance, while a condition can only be vague, something that may occur and may not occur. The fāʾ entered only because of the vagueness in الَّذِي together with its ṣila (relative clause) being a verb. This shows that the verse is not about sins and acts of obedience, as the people of deviation said; moreover, the wording is مَا أَصَابَك ("what befalls you"), and He did not say مَا أصبت ("what you do").
His saying {وأرسلناك للنَّاس رَسُولا}: رَسُولا is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "possessing a message" (ذَا رِسَالَة). شهيدا is tafsīr (specification), and it has been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial); and like it is وَكيلا.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t: His saying {طَاعَة}: nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); its implied form is "and they say: our affair is obedience" (وَيَقُولُونَ أمرنَا طَاعَة). In speech, the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) is permitted.

mekki-muskil:82-82.t: His saying {أَفلا يتدبرون الْقُرْآن}, His saying ليدبروا آيَاته, and its parallels in the Book of Allah the Exalted — all of it indicates the urging to seek the meanings of the Quran and to search into its benefits, its parables, its interpretation, its implied elements, the wonders of what it intends, its rulings, and its abrogating and abrogated [verses], among similar branches of its knowledge that cannot be counted. And there is no way to come to know the realities of any of that except by knowing its i'rab (grammatical analysis) and the changes of its vowels and its word-forms.

mekki-muskil:83-83.t:
His saying {لاتبعتم الشَّيْطَان إِلَّا قَلِيلا}: قَلِيلا is accusative as an exception from the plural pronoun latent in أذاعوا. It has also been said: from the kāf and mīm in عَلَيْكُم, on the implied form "were it not for Allah's favour upon you in sending His Messenger among you so that you believed in him, you would have disbelieved, except a few of you" — namely those who were upon faith before the sending of the Messenger, peace be upon him. After لَوْلَا a mubtadaʾ (subject) occurs and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; so فضل is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, and making it overt is not permitted according to Sībawayh.
His saying {تَحِيَّة}: its pattern is تفعلة and its original form is تحيية; the vowel of the yāʾ was cast onto the ḥāʾ, and it was assimilated into the second [yāʾ].

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {الله لَا إِلَه إِلَّا هُوَ}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); لَا إِلَه is a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause is the khabar of الله; and إِلَّا هُوَ is a badal (substitute) for the position of لَا إِلَه.

mekki-muskil:88-88.t: His saying {فئتين}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in لكم, as you say مَالك قَائِما ("why are you standing?").

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His saying {كَمَا كفرُوا}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a disbelief like their disbelief" (كفرا مثل كفرهم).

mekki-muskil:90-90.t:
His saying {إِلَّا الَّذين يصلونَ}: in the position of the accusative as an exception from the hāʾ and mīm in واقتلوهم.
His saying {حصرت صُدُورهمْ}: حصرت cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative latent pronoun in جاءوكم unless you imply قد with it; if you do not imply قد, it is an imprecation (duʿāʾ), as you say لعن الله الْكَافِر ("may Allah curse the disbeliever"). It has also been said that حصرت is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. As for whoever reads حصرة with tanwīn, making it a noun, it is a ḥāl from the nominative latent pronoun in جاءوكم; and if it were made genitive as a naʿt of قوم, it would be permitted.
His saying {أَن يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:92-92.t:
His saying {أَن يقتل}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of كَانَ; إِلَّا خطأ is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); and like it is أَن in إِلَّا أَن يصدقُوا.
His saying {فَتَحْرِير رَقَبَة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; its implied form is "then upon him is the freeing of a slave" (فَعَلَيهِ تَحْرِير رَقَبَة). ودية مسلمة is like it, and likewise فَصِيَام شَهْرَيْن, i.e. "then upon him is a fast of two months."
His saying {تَوْبَة من الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. The nominative is permitted in speech on the implied form "that is a repentance" (ذَلِك تَوْبَة).

mekki-muskil:95-95.t:
His saying {غير أولي الضَّرَر}: whoever makes غير accusative does so as an exception from القاعدين, or, if you wish, from الْمُؤمنِينَ; or, if you wish, you make it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from القاعدين, i.e. "those who sit are not equal in the state of their health." Whoever makes غير nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of القاعدين, because they are not specified — no particular people are intended by them — so they became like an indefinite, and it was permitted to describe them with غير; and the ḥāl from them was permitted because their wording is the wording of a definite. Its parallel has already passed in the accusative and genitive of غير المغضوب. It is better for the nominative in غير to be as a badal (substitute) for القاعدين. Abū Ḥaywa read غير in the genitive as a naʿt of الْمُؤمنِينَ, and it has been said it is a badal for الْمُؤمنِينَ.
His saying {وكلا وعد الله الْحسنى}: كلا is accusative by وعد.
His saying {أجرا}: accusative by فضل, or, if you wish, as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His saying {دَرَجَات}: accusative as a badal (substitute) for أجر.

mekki-muskil:97-97.t:
His saying {ظالمي أنفسهم}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in تَوَفَّاهُم; the nūn was dropped because of the genitive construct.
His saying {فيمَ كُنْتُم}: the alif of ما was dropped because the preposition entered upon it, to distinguish between the declarative and the interrogative: the alif is dropped in the interrogative and kept in the declarative. Like it are عَم يتساءلون عَن النبأ الْعَظِيم, لم أَذِنت, فبم تبشرون and the like.

mekki-muskil:98-98.t:
His saying {إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ}: an exception in the position of the accusative from إِن الَّذين تَوَفَّاهُم الْمَلَائِكَة.
His saying {لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ; likewise وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلا.

mekki-muskil:100-100.t: His saying {مُهَاجرا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يخرج.

mekki-muskil:101-101.t:
His saying {أَن تقصرُوا من الصَّلَاة}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition; its implied form is فِي أَن تقصرُوا ("in shortening").
His saying {عدوا}: it is singular, though what precedes it is plural, only because it is in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun); its implied form is "they are possessors of enmity towards you" (كَانُوا لكم ذَوي عَدَاوَة).

mekki-muskil:103-103.t: His saying {قيَاما وقعودا}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent pronoun in اذْكروا; likewise وعَلى جنوبكم, because it is in the place of "lying down" (مضطجعين).

mekki-muskil:105-105.t: His saying {إِنَّا أنزلنَا إِلَيْك الْكتاب بِالْحَقِّ}: بِالْحَقِّ is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكتاب, and it is an emphatic ḥāl. It is not permitted for أنزلنَا to be made transitive to it by a particle, because it has already been made transitive to one object without a particle and to another with a particle.

mekki-muskil:109-109.t: His saying {هَا أَنْتُم هَؤُلَاءِ جادلتم}: it is like His saying ثمَّ أَنْتُم هَؤُلَاءِ تقتلون, whose explanation and the disagreement about it have already passed; except that here you do not make جادلتم a ḥāl (circumstantial) unless you imply قد with it.

mekki-muskil:114-114.t:
His saying {إِلَّا من أَمر بِصَدقَة}: من is in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) if you take نَجوَاهُمْ as a noun for what they converse about secretly. The meaning of our saying "disconnected exception" and "the exception that is not of the same kind as the first" is one and the same thing. If you take نَجوَاهُمْ in the sense of their group who converse secretly, من is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for نَجوَاهُمْ, and it is a badal of part for whole.
His saying {ابْتِغَاء مرضات الله}: ابْتِغَاء is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:115-115.t: His saying {وَسَاءَتْ مصيرا}: accusative as tafsīr (specification).

mekki-muskil:122-122.t: His saying {قيلا}: also accusative as tafsīr (specification). One says قيلا, قولا and قالا with the same meaning.

mekki-muskil:123-123.t: His saying {لَيْسَ بأمانيكم}: the noun (ism) of لَيْسَ is a pronoun implied in it, referring to what the idol-worshippers claimed — that they would not be resurrected — and to what the Jews and Christians said: "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." So Allah revealed: "That is not according to your wishes, O idol-worshippers, nor according to the wishes of the People of the Book." The meaning is: what will come to be of your affairs on the Day of Resurrection is not what you wish for. It has also been said that its implied form is "the reward of Allah is not according to your wishes" (لَيْسَ ثَوَاب الله بأمانيكم).

mekki-muskil:125-125.t: His saying {حَنِيفا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in اتبع.

mekki-muskil:127-127.t:
His saying {وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُم}: ما is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the name of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "Allah gives you a ruling, and what is recited in the Book gives you a ruling," namely the Quran.
His saying {وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ}: genitive, conjoined to يتامى النِّسَاء; and like it is أَن in His saying وَأَن تقوموا. The implied form is: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning women, and the Quran that is recited to you concerning the orphan women, and concerning the oppressed among the children, and concerning your standing for the orphans with justice, also gives you a ruling" — and that is what Allah related in mentioning the orphans at the beginning of the sura. Al-Farrāʾ said: ما in وَمَا يُتْلَى is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the pronoun in فِيهِنَّ; that is not permitted according to the Basrans, because it is conjoining an overt noun to a genitive pronoun. It has also been said that ما is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is "gives you a ruling," which is omitted.
His saying {وترغبون أَن تنكحوهن}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition; its implied form is فِي أَن تنكحوهن ("[desire] to marry them").

mekki-muskil:128-128.t:
His saying {وَإِن امْرَأَة}: nominative according to Sībawayh by an implied verb; its implied form is "and if a woman fears, fears…" (وان خَافت امْرَأَة خَافت), and its explanation has already passed. It is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to others.
His saying {أَن يصالحا}: like أَن تنكحوهن, i.e. فِي أَن يصالحا ("in their making peace").
His saying {صلحا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the implied form "except that they make peace between them, so that the matter is set right with a settlement" (إِلَّا أَن يصالحا بَينهمَا فيصلح الْأَمر صلحا).

mekki-muskil:131-131.t: His saying {أَن اتَّقوا الله}: i.e. بِأَن اتَّقوا الله ("that you fear Allah").

mekki-muskil:135-135.t:
His saying {شُهَدَاء}: a naʿt (adjective) of قوامين or a second khabar (predicate); it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in قوامين.
His saying {أَن تعدلوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative on the omission of the preposition, i.e. فِي أَن لَا تعدلوا ("in not acting justly"), with لا implied.
His saying {وَإِن تلووا}: whoever reads it with ḍamma on the lām and a single wāw (تلُوا) — it may be from ولي يلي, its original form being توليوا; then it was weakened by dropping the wāw because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, then the vowel of the yāʾ was cast onto the lām and the yāʾ was dropped because of its being vowelless with the vowelless wāw after it. It may also be from لوى يلوي, its original form being تلووا as in the reading of the majority, except that he replaced the first wāw with a hamza because it has ḍamma, and cast its vowel onto the lām, so it became ḍamma-vowelled.
His saying {بهما}: dual, though what precedes it affirms one of two things by أو. أو according to al-Akhfash is in the place of the wāw ("and"). It has been said that its implied form is "whether the two disputants are both rich or both poor, Allah is more worthy of them both." It has been said that it is like His saying وَله أَخ أَو أُخْت فَلِكُل وَاحِد مِنْهُمَا. It has been said: since the meaning is "Allah is more worthy of the richness of the rich and the poverty of the poor," the pronoun was referred back to both of them. And it has been said: the pronoun refers to both only because no particular poor man and no particular rich man was intended.

mekki-muskil:140-140.t: His saying {أَن إِذا سَمِعْتُمْ}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) according to the reading of whoever reads نُزِّل with ḍamma; as for whoever reads it with fatḥa (نَزَّل), أَن is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of نزل.

mekki-muskil:142-142.t: His saying {كسَالَى}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in قَامُوا; likewise يراءون is also a ḥāl, and like it is وَلَا يذكرُونَ; and like it is مذبذبين, a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in يذكرُونَ. The meaning of مذبذبين is "wavering, neither with the Muslims nor with the disbelievers."

mekki-muskil:146-146.t: His saying {فَأُولَئِك مَعَ الْمُؤمنِينَ}: أُولَئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; its implied form is "so those are believers along with the believers" (فَأُولَئِك مُؤمنُونَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ). «[Translator's note: the source writes the last word as الْمُؤْمِنُونَ, in the nominative, after مَعَ.]»

mekki-muskil:147-147.t: His saying {مَا يفعل الله}: ما is interrogative, in the position of the accusative by يفعل.

mekki-muskil:148-148.t: His saying {إِلَّا من ظلم}: من is in the position of the accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first. It may also be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) according to the meaning, because the meaning of the statement is "Allah does not love that anyone should publicize evil except one who has been wronged"; so من is made a badal for the implied أحد.

mekki-muskil:150-150.t: His saying {بَين ذَلِك سَبِيلا}: ذَلِك is used as a demonstrative for one, for two and for a group; therefore it came as a demonstrative after two things in this verse, namely "we believe in some" and "we disbelieve in some." Its meaning is: they want to take a path between faith and disbelief.

mekki-muskil:153-153.t: His saying {جهرة}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in قَالُوا, i.e. they said that openly. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "an open seeing" (رُؤْيَة جهرة).

mekki-muskil:154-154.t: His saying {سجدا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in ادخُلُوا.

mekki-muskil:155-155.t: His saying {فبمَا نقضهم ميثاقهم}: ما is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and نقضهم is genitive by the bāʾ. It has also been said that ما is an indefinite noun in the position of the genitive and نقضهم is a badal (substitute) for ما.

mekki-muskil:156-156.t: His saying {بهتانا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial); it has also been said: a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:157-157.t:
His saying {إِلَّا اتِّبَاع الظَّن}: accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first. In speech it may be made nominative as a badal (substitute) for the position of من علم, because من is redundant and علم is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying {يَقِينا}: there are two implied forms for it. It has been said: "Allah said this as a certain saying" (قَالَ الله هَذَا قولا يَقِينا); and it has been said: "and they did not know it with certain knowledge" (وَمَا علموه علما يَقِينا).

mekki-muskil:160-160.t: His saying {كثيرا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "much turning away" (صدودا كثيرا).

mekki-muskil:162-162.t:
His saying {والمقيمين الصَّلَاة}: it is accusative as praise (al-madḥ) according to Sībawayh. Al-Kisāʾī said it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ما in His saying بِمَا أنزل إِلَيْك; that is far-fetched, because the meaning becomes "they believe in what was revealed to you and in those who establish the prayer." It is only permissible if you make "those who establish the prayer" the angels, so that you are informing about those firmly grounded in knowledge and about those who believe in what Allah revealed to Muhammad, and they believe in the angels, whose attribute is establishing the prayer, because of His saying يسبحون اللَّيْل وَالنَّهَار لَا يفترون. It has been said that المقيمين is conjoined to the kāf in قبلك, i.e. "and from before those who establish the prayer"; that is far-fetched, because it is conjoining an overt noun to a genitive pronoun. It has been said that it is conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm in مِنْهُم; both of these views involve conjoining an overt noun to a genitive pronoun. It has been said that it is conjoined to قبل, as though He said "and before those who establish [the prayer]" (وَقبل المقيمين), then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. Whoever makes المقيمين accusative as praise makes the khabar (predicate) of الراسخين be يُؤمنُونَ; if he makes the khabar أُولَئِكَ سنؤتيهم, the accusative of المقيمين as praise is not permitted, because praise comes only after the statement is complete.
His saying {والمؤتون الزَّكَاة}: nominative according to Sībawayh as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It has been said: on an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and they are those who give" (وهم المؤتون). It has been said that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in مقيمين; it has been said: to the latent pronoun in يُؤمنُونَ; and it has been said: to الراسخين.

mekki-muskil:163-163.t: His saying {كَمَا أَوْحَينَا}: the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a revealing such as" (إيحاء كَمَا).

mekki-muskil:164-164.t: His saying {ورسلا قد قصصناهم}: accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and We related messengers whom We have related to you before" (وقصصنا رسلًا قد قصصناهم عَلَيْك من قبل). It has also been said that it is construed according to the meaning, conjoined to what precedes it, because the meaning of أَوْحَينَا is "We sent"; so its implied form becomes "We sent you [and] messengers" (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاك رسلًا).

mekki-muskil:165-165.t: His saying {رسلًا مبشرين}: رسلًا is a badal (substitute) for ورسلا. It has been said that it is accusative on an implied verb, i.e. "We sent messengers bearing good tidings" (أرسلنَا رسلًا مبشرين). It has been said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and مبشرين and منذرين are a naʿt (adjective) of رسل.

mekki-muskil:170-170.t: His saying {فآمنوا خيرا لكم}: خيرا is accusative according to Sībawayh on an implied verb; its implied form is "come to what is better for you" (ائْتُوا خيرا لكم), because آمنُوا indicates bringing them out of one matter and bringing them into what is better for them than it. Al-Farrāʾ said it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "so believe with a belief better for you" (فآمنوا إِيمَانًا خيرا لكم). Abū ʿUbayda said it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied كان, its implied form being "so believe, it will be better for you" (فآمنوا يكن خيرا لكم), i.e. faith will be better for you.

mekki-muskil:171-171.t:
His saying {وَلَا تَقولُوا ثَلَاثَة}: ثَلَاثَة is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); its implied form is "our gods are three" (آلِهَتنَا ثَلَاثَة).
His saying {انْتَهوا خيرا لكم}: خيرا according to Sībawayh is accusative by an implied verb whose overt expression is abandoned, because when you say "desist" you bring him out of one matter and into another, so it is as though you said "come to what is better for you" (أئت خيرا لَك). Al-Farrāʾ said it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "desist with a desisting better for you" (انْتَهوا انْتِهَاء خيرا لكم). Abū ʿUbayda said it is the khabar of an omitted كان, its implied form being "desist, it will be better for you" (انْتَهوا يكن خيرا لكم). It is related from some of the Kufans that its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and that is far-fetched.
His saying {إِنَّمَا الله إِلَه وَاحِد}: ما restrains (kāffa) أنّ from governing; الله is a mubtadaʾ, إله is its khabar, and وَاحِد is a naʿt; its implied form is "Allah is only alone in His divinity." It has been said that وَاحِد is a tawkīd (emphasis), in the status of لَا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلَهَيْنِ. It is also possible for إِلَه to be a badal (substitute) for الله and وَاحِد its khabar, its implied form being "the one worshipped is only one." سُبْحَانَهُ is accusative as a maṣdar.
His saying {أَن يكون}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition; its implied form is "glory be to Him above having" (سُبْحَانَهُ على أَن يكون) or "from having" (وَمن أَن يكون), i.e. as a declaration of His exaltation above that and His freedom from it.
His saying وَكيلا: accusative as bayān (clarification), or, if you wish, as a ḥāl. The meaning of وَكيل is "sufficient for His friends."

mekki-muskil:172-172.t: His saying {أَن يكون عبدا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, i.e. من أَن يكون ("from being").

mekki-muskil:175-175.t: His saying {ويهديهم إِلَيْهِ صراطا}: صراطا is accusative on an implied verb; its implied form is "He makes known to them a path" (يعرفهُمْ صراطا), and يهْدِيهم points to what is omitted. It may also be the second mafʿūl (object) of يهديهم, its implied form being "and He guides them on a straight path to His reward and recompense."

mekki-muskil:176-176.t:
His saying {فَإِن كَانَتَا اثْنَتَيْنِ}: the pronoun in كَانَتَا is dual, although only one [sister] was mentioned before, only because it is construed according to the meaning; for its implied form according to al-Akhfash is "if those he leaves are two" (فَإِن كَانَ من ترك اثْنَتَيْنِ), then the pronoun was made dual according to the meaning of من.
His saying {أَن تضلوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by يبين, since its meaning is "Allah makes clear to you error so that you avoid it." It has been said that لا is implied, omitted from the statement, its implied form being "Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray" (يبين الله لكم لِئَلَّا تضلوا). And it has been said that its meaning is "out of dislike that you go astray" (كَرَاهَة أَن تضلوا), so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
